note: Trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column on every insert/update. Touches no table, takes no lock on orders.

Add nullable column customer_id_new bigint (metadata only, no rewrite) and the sync trigger, in one transaction. Locks are taken with a short lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind us for more than a few hundred ms.
Backfill existing rows in batches of 20,000 ids, committing each batch (short row locks, no table lock; the app never updates orders). Every row inserted from now on is filled by the trigger.
Clean up the dead tuples left by the backfill (plain VACUUM, does not block reads or writes).
Prove the new column is NOT NULL without a long lock: add a NOT VALID check (brief lock, retried), then VALIDATE it (scans under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block the app).
Safety check: stop the plan if any row's new value differs from the old one.

Swap in one short transaction (lock retried): SET NOT NULL (no scan, the validated check proves it), drop the check and the trigger, drop the old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id. All metadata-only. The app keeps using the name customer_id, so no deploy is needed.
Verify: orders.customer_id is bigint NOT NULL.
